messages.subject: video transect data
parts:
Hello List,=0D=0AI'm fairly new to the list but have looked through t=
he archives and did not=0D=0Afind any postings on this topic so far..=
.=0D=0A =0D=0AI am interested in applying distance sampling methods t=
o the design and=0D=0Aanalysis of video transects for analysing the d=
istribution and abundance of=0D=0Aseabed fauna and would be like to m=
ake contact with anyone engaged in=0D=0Asimilar work if there are any=
of you out there!? I imagine that the=0D=0Aprinciples are similar t=
o those for detecting stationary terrestrial fauna=0D=0Aor plants so =
this would also be of interest. =0D=0A =0D=0ATypically we use a down=
ward facing camera from a remotely operated vehicle=0D=0A(ROV) platfo=
rm which is flown at a fairly constant altitude above the=0D=0Aseabed=
. We are able to count objects such as corals (treat as clusters?),=
=0D=0Aurchins, starfish etc. that occur within the field of view as =
we move along=0D=0Athe transect and can also identify typical seabed =
habitats (strata?) from=0D=0Athis data. We also have information fro=
m acoustic remote sensing which may=0D=0Abe useful in stratifying the=
survey area and since we are surveying the deep=0D=0Asea, cost-effec=
tive survey designs are very important due to costly shiptime=0D=0Aan=
d equipment hire. =0D=0A =0D=0AFrom my initial reading it seems that=
some of the methods and applications=0D=0Aof distance sampling are r=
elevant, however I'd appreciate any assistance=0D=0Athat more experie=
nced users of the techniques can offer.=0D=0A =0D=0AMany thanks, =
